messages.subject: Basics Unmark guide
parts:
Hello friends, 
I am very new to R and overall statistics. I want to learn occupancy modelling using R. 

I have read a bit about occupancy modelling and conceptually now I am fairly clear with it. 
However I dont know where and I how to start. 

I have a data-set of track counts over short transects (250m). I used 12 transects per site. I worked on total 6 sites. 
I want to estimate species relative occupancy and compare species between sites. 
Is it possible to do it in Unmark? 

Can anyone provide me with basic example? 
How should the dataset look like? 
And how can I estimate species for such a multiple species dataset. 
Most of the occupancy estimates I came across were for single species. 

Will be glad for help and guidance. 

Thanks in advance. 
Hemant

messages.author: 527d9b3ec7deff2d
messages.subject: Re: Basics Unmark guide
parts:
The vignettes should have most of what you need and are very helpful: http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/unmarked/vignettes/

Multi-species data sets can be analyzed with for loops in R (iterating through each species, fitting separate models, and saving/printing output) or specifying "species" as a fixed or random effect in your model structure.  If you want the latter, unmarked cannot handle random effects so you'd be relegated to BUGS.
